column1: # GitHub Actions whose code was replaced by malware for a time. Section 5 lists each project whose
# workflows (.github/workflows/*.yml and *.yaml) name one in a uses: line. Whether a project was hit
# depends on whether its workflows ran in the window, which no file on this machine shows, so a match
# is a project to check, never a compromised machine.
# One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   action  owner/repo as the source names it. Compared without regard to case, as GitHub does
#   refs    the refs that ran the malware: tags or branches, as shell patterns separated by spaces
#           (* any characters, ? one, [1-9] one of a range), each matched against the whole ref, or
#           * for every ref. A pattern starting with ! is a ref that did not
#   shas    the full commit SHAs the source lists as malicious, separated by commas, or -
#   pin     safe: a pin to any other full commit SHA did not run the malware, as the source says.
#           unsafe: every pin ran it too, as the source says
#   window  when it was compromised, read after "compromised": "on 14 and 15 March 2025"
#   source  the primary source's https link: a GitHub advisory, the maintainer's post, or a named
#           security research firm's post
#   fix     shown under each use found: what to pin it to or whether to remove it, from the source
# tj-actions/changed-files: GitHub's advisory names the malicious commit and the range up to 45.0.7, every
# tag there was then; tags were restored on 15 March 2025. reviewdog/action-setup: its v1 tag only;
# the five reviewdog actions the advisory names ran it whatever their version or pin. xygeni-action: the
# v5 tag, moved to 4bf1d4e1, and the advisory's safe pin. trivy-action: every tag but 0.35.0 (the
# v-prefixed ones were published after), and a pin to a commit before 9 April 2025 fetched the
# compromised setup-trivy, so no pin is called safe. setup-trivy: its seven tags, v0.2.0 to v0.2.6.
# kics-github-action: Wiz lists its 35 tags (every one starts with v) and their malicious commits; Wiz
# names Checkmarx/ast-github-action too, but only tag 2.3.28 is reported and no commits, so it has no
# line. actions-cool: StepSecurity lists all 53 and 15 tags (every one starts with v) and their
# malicious commits; SafeDep found the same tags still malicious, and new repositories infected through
# them, from 20 to 24 September 2026.
# action
tj-actions/changed-files
column7: Its tags were restored after the attack. Pin it to a full commit SHA.

column1: reviewdog/action-shellcheck
column7: Every version and pin of it ran the compromised reviewdog/action-setup@v1 in that window.

column1: reviewdog/action-composite-template
column7: Every version and pin of it ran the compromised reviewdog/action-setup@v1 in that window.

column7: Every version and pin of it ran the compromised reviewdog/action-setup@v1 in that window.

column1: reviewdog/action-ast-grep
column7: Every version and pin of it ran the compromised reviewdog/action-setup@v1 in that window.

column1: reviewdog/action-typos
column7: Every version and pin of it ran the compromised reviewdog/action-setup@v1 in that window.

column1: reviewdog/action-setup
column7: Its v1 tag was restored after the attack. Pin it to a full commit SHA.

column1: xygeni/xygeni-action
column7: Pin it to 13c6ed2797df7d85749864e2cbcf09c893f43b23, its v6.4.0, as Xygeni advises.

column1: aquasecurity/trivy-action
column7: Pin it to the full commit SHA of v0.35.0 or later. A pin to a commit from before 9 April 2025 ran the compromised setup-trivy then too.

column1: aquasecurity/setup-trivy
column7: Pin it to the full commit SHA of v0.2.6 or later, published again with safe code.

column1: Checkmarx/kics-github-action
column7: Pin it to the full commit SHA of a release published after the attack.

column1: actions-cool/issues-helper
column7: Remove it. Every tag was moved to a malicious commit, and in September 2026 the tags still ran it.

column1: actions-cool/maintain-one-comment
column7: Remove it. Every tag was moved to a malicious commit.
